newsitem.title: USA: Merisel in pact to restructure debt.
newsitem.headline: Merisel in pact to restructure debt.

text.p: Computer components distributor Merisel Inc on Monday said it had reached an agreement in principle with holders of more than 75 percent of its 12.5 percent senior notes to convert the securities to common stock.

The company said it also had agreements in principle with participating lenders in the revolving credit agreement, 11.5 percent senior notes, and subordinated notes issued by its subsidiary, Merisel Americas Inc.
The company said the agreements are included in its 10-K, which it said was filed earlier Monday.
Merisel said the pacts would eliminate $125 million of 12.5 percent senior note obligations, restructure about $155 million of debt and amend certain covenants.
Because of the large number of shares to be issued in the exchange, the company said it may consider a reverse stock split.

Under the agreements, holders of the 12.5-percent senior notes would exchange their notes for 80 percent of the post-restructuring outstanding shares of common stock, about 120.3 million shares based on 30.1 million shares now outstanding, Merisel said.
Stockholders as of the exchange date would receive warrants to buy 17.5 percent of the then-outstanding, post-restructuring common stock, or about 26.4 million shares, the company said.
It said the warrants would be exercisable for seven years and would be issued in two separate tranches at prices of about $1.43 and $1.74 a share based on the number of shares currently outstanding.
The company said the exchange of debt for equity requires the consent of remaining debtholders of Merisel Americas and of stockholders.
It said if approval cannot be obtained from all noteholders, it and the noteholders have agreed to complete the conversion through a prepackaged plan of reorganization under Chapter 11.

"We believe that the debt restructuring will enhance the long-term equity value of the company and relieve Merisel from financial restrictions that have inhibited the company from achieving greater profitability," the company said in a release.
